mods.name: VoxelCam
mods.description: Adds features to make in-game screenshots easier to handle, including editing and uploading to image hosts.

releases.notes:
Capture stopped being one key. There is a dial on `F2`, bursts, and screenshots VoxelCam takes by
itself when something worth keeping happens.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API
- Java 25, the runtime the Minecraft launcher already ships with (no launcher changes needed)

## A dial on the shutter

Hold `F2` and a dial opens: aim at **Screenshot**, **Big Screenshot** or **Burst**, and let go.
Tapping `F2` still takes an ordinary screenshot, so nothing changes if you never hold it. The dial's
outer ring sets the burst length and the oversized size without leaving it.

## Burst capture

A run of consecutive frames from one press, for the moment too short to time by hand. The manager
lists a burst as a single entry you can expand, and any frame inside it can be promoted to the one
that represents the group.

## Screenshots you did not take

VoxelCam now catches the moments you would have missed: when you earn an advancement, when a boss
bar empties, when you die, and the first time you arrive in a dimension. Each screenshot records
what caused it, so the manager can tell you afterwards why a file you did not ask for exists.

All four are on by default and each can be switched off. No more than one is taken every ten
seconds, so a run of advancements is one screenshot rather than five — the interval is adjustable.

This works with content mods without knowing anything about them: an advancement from any mod
arrives through the same vanilla system, so there is no per-mod adapter and nothing to keep up to
date.

The rule throughout is that a capture at the wrong moment is worse than none. If you open your
inventory before the shot lands, it is dropped rather than saved ten seconds late — and the attempt
does not spend your cooldown.

## Settings that stay put

Burst length and oversized size now survive a restart. There is a settings screen behind the gear
button in the manager, reachable from Mod Menu too if you have it, covering the full burst range and
every big-screenshot preset — more than the dial's five-value ladders reach.

## Fixes

Two UI overlaps in the manager, and the capture dial cancels cleanly on `Escape`.

mods.name: VoxelCam
mods.description: Adds features to make in-game screenshots easier to handle, including editing and uploading to image hosts.

releases.notes:
Screenshots now carry the context they were taken in, and the manager can sort and filter on it.
Everything is written into the PNG itself, so it survives copying, renaming and sharing — there is
no sidecar file to lose.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API
- Java 25, the runtime the Minecraft launcher already ships with (no launcher changes needed)

## Where a screenshot was taken

Every new capture records its dimension and coordinates, and the name of the world or server it came
from. The manager shows the location under the preview. The server's *address* is deliberately not
recorded — a screenshot you share should not carry one.

Captures also record which mods were loaded, and the active Iris shader pack if there is one.
Infrastructure is filtered out, so the tag reads as a line of text rather than a wall of Fabric API
module ids.

## Sorting and favourites

The manager sorts by date, name, file size or image dimensions, ascending or descending, from a
button beside the search bar. Screenshots can be starred, and a filter narrows the list to just
those. Starring writes into the PNG and restores the file's timestamp afterwards, so a favourite
does not jump to the top of a newest-first list.

## Older screenshots

Screenshots taken before 2.3.0 — or by vanilla `F2`, or another mod — have no embedded context.
They still list, sort by date, name and size, preview and share exactly as before; only the location
line and the provenance tag are missing, and they can still be starred.

## Elsewhere

The camera button is now on the pause menu as well as the title screen, in the same row of icon
buttons.

## Fixes

Twenty-three fixes closed alongside the features, all of them found by an audit of the 2.2.0 code
rather than reported in play.

The ones most likely to have affected you: a failed screenshot save no longer leaves a truncated
`.png` behind; a rename or delete the filesystem refuses now says so instead of appearing to work; a
screenshot can be renamed to a different capitalisation; the rename dialog keeps keyboard focus when
opened with the keyboard; and the manager's selection follows a file across a rename rather than
jumping to the top of the list.

Oversized capture is sturdier under failure — a readback that fails or stalls can no longer restore
the window while the GPU is still reading from it. Non-English systems are handled properly
throughout: capture names always use ASCII digits and the ISO year, and `/bigscreenshot imax` is
accepted whatever your system locale does to capital letters.

The manager also got materially cheaper. Full-size previews are now capped rather than accumulating
for every screenshot you look at, file facts are cached instead of being re-read from disk for every
visible row on every frame, and the sort no longer re-reads each file once per comparison.

mods.name: VoxelCam
mods.description: Adds features to make in-game screenshots easier to handle, including editing and uploading to image hosts.

releases.notes:
VoxelCam now runs on Minecraft 26.2. Nothing about the mod itself has changed — this release exists
to follow Minecraft, which stopped obfuscating its code and rewrote how the interface is drawn.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API
- Java 25, the runtime the Minecraft launcher already ships with (no launcher changes needed)

## Upgrading

**2.2.0 will not load on 1.21.11, and 2.1.0 will not load on 26.2.** Minecraft 26.1 was the first
release with unobfuscated code, and mods built for either side of that line are not interchangeable.
If you are staying on 1.21.11, keep [2.1.0](https://github.com/thatapplefreak/VoxelCam/releases/tag/v2.1.0).

Your screenshots are untouched by any of this — they are ordinary PNGs in your screenshots folder,
and the manager reads whatever is there.

## The camera button moved

26.2 added a Friends button to the title screen, next to the language and accessibility icons. The
camera has joined that row rather than sitting off on its own beside Quit Game, and the row stays
centred with four buttons in it the way it did with three.

Everything else is where it was. `H` opens the screenshot manager, `F2` takes a screenshot,
`Shift`+`F2` takes an oversized one, and `/bigscreenshot` still sets the size.

## Under the hood

Yarn, the mapping set every Fabric mod was written against, stopped being published after 1.21.11 —
Minecraft ships readable names now, so it is no longer needed. The mod moved to Mojang's own names,
and its interface was rewritten for 26.x, which replaced immediate drawing with a model where
screens describe themselves and are painted afterwards. The oversized capture needed the most care:
the frame method it hooks was split in two, and the point where a finished frame is handed to the
screen changed entirely.

None of that is visible in-game, which is the point.

## Tests

This release adds the project's first test suites: 82 unit tests, plus four tests that drive a real
Minecraft client and check the title screen button, the screenshot manager, sharing, and both
ordinary and oversized capture. Both run in CI and have to pass before a jar is built.

mods.name: VoxelCam
mods.description: Adds features to make in-game screenshots easier to handle, including editing and uploading to image hosts.

releases.notes:
Oversized screenshots are back. 2.0.0 shipped with Shift+F2 reporting that big screenshots were not
supported; this release restores them.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 1.21.11
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API
- Java 21, the runtime the Minecraft launcher already ships with (no launcher changes needed)

## Big screenshots

Hold `Shift` and press `F2` to capture a frame far larger than your window — a 4K or 8K wallpaper
from a 1080p game. The shot lands in your screenshots folder like any other and shows up in the
manager straight away.

Set the size with `/bigscreenshot`, or `/bs` for short. It takes:

- **Presets** — `hd`, `fhd`, `4k`, `8k`, and `imax` (10000x7000, the old LiteLoader preset)
- **A multiple of your window** — `2x`, `4x`, `8x`. These keep your window's aspect ratio, so the
  shot is framed exactly like what is on screen
- **Exact dimensions** — `3840x2160`, `1000x1000`, anything you like

Run `/bigscreenshot` with no argument to see the current setting. The size lasts for the session and
is not written to a config file. Requests larger than your GPU allows are scaled down to fit, with
both dimensions reduced together so the framing is preserved, and the limit is reported in chat.

Your HUD setting is respected: whatever is on screen is what gets captured. Big screenshots are
taken in-world only, with no menu open, and the game will pause noticeably while a very large image
is read back and encoded.

## Fixes

- The camera button on the title screen no longer stays fully opaque while the rest of the menu
  fades in.

## Licence

VoxelCam is released under the **GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0**. Modpack inclusion is
permitted; modifications to VoxelCam itself must be released under the same licence. The full terms
ship inside the jar under `META-INF/`, and live in `COPYING` and `COPYING.LESSER` in the repository.

releases.notes:
VoxelCam is now a Fabric mod for Minecraft 1.21.11. This is a ground-up port of the old LiteLoader
mod, and it changes how sharing works.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 1.21.11
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API
- Java 21, the runtime the Minecraft launcher already ships with (no launcher changes needed)

## Screenshot manager

Open it with `H` in-game, or from the camera button on the title screen. Search your screenshots,
browse them with thumbnails and a large preview, and rename (`F2`) or delete (`Del`) without leaving
the game.

## Sharing without accounts

The Share menu needs no account, API key, or login:

- **Save a copy…** — your platform's native Save dialog, so you can drop a screenshot straight into a
  synced iCloud/Dropbox/OneDrive folder
- **Show in file manager** — reveals the file in Finder/Explorer
- **Copy file path**
- **Get a share link** — uploads to [catbox.moe](https://catbox.moe) and copies the link

## Removed

Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, and Imgur posting are gone, along with auto-upload on capture and the
built-in image editor. They depended on OAuth credentials or a LiteLoader-era rendering stack that
does not exist in modern Minecraft. The old implementation is preserved in this repository's Git
history.

Oversized "big screenshot" capture (Shift+F2) is not yet ported and reports that it is unsupported.

## Licence

VoxelCam 2.0.0 onward is released under the **GNU Lesser General Public License
v3.0**. Modpack inclusion is permitted; modifications to VoxelCam itself must be
released under the same licence. The full terms ship inside the jar under
`META-INF/`, and live in `COPYING` and `COPYING.LESSER` in the repository.
